domains.backend: Request handling, APIs, databases, queues, caching.
domains.data: Transformation, parsing, serialization, pipelines, file I/O.
domains.ml: Model loading, inference, embeddings, training utilities.
domains.infra: Deployment, config management, logging, monitoring, health checks.
domains.universal: Pure utilities with no domain dependency (string ops, retry, math, date handling). If a widget could reasonably belong to two domains, it belongs here.

general_notes: Single responsibility - one widget does one thing. No global state. No project-specific code, hardcoded paths, credentials, or environment-specific values. Expose variation points as constructor parameters or function arguments - no hardcoded thresholds, colors, sizes, or behavior flags. All dependencies must be declared in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies. Widgets cannot depend on other widgets - they must be fully self-contained. If you need logic from another widget, copy it into src/ directly. Examples must run and exit cleanly with no user input, no network calls, and no external services or API keys - use fake/hardcoded data. The widget's own declared dependencies are fine and will be installed by the validator before the example runs. Do not modify library_notes - it is managed by Cartograph and will be restored on checkin.

language_notes.python: Use pytest for all tests - no unittest. Type hints required on all public functions. No __init__.py in tests/. No if __name__ == '__main__' blocks in src/ files. Imports ordered: stdlib, third-party, local.
language_notes.javascript: Use vitest for all tests. No console.log() in src/ files. Use named exports, not default exports. Test filename must match src filename exactly. Only test/expect/describe/vi are global - all other imports must be explicit. Plain JS: files use .js, examples run with node and exit cleanly. React (when react is in dependencies): components are PascalCase .jsx, hooks are camelCase .js starting with 'use'. Import render/screen/fireEvent/act explicitly from '@testing-library/react'. Components must render cleanly via react-dom/server renderToString with no browser APIs (window, document, localStorage) in the initial render path. Hook examples must wrap the hook in a local demo component for renderToString - hooks cannot be rendered directly. Usage hints: you may optionally include examples/usage_hint.* with real integration code that requires a browser or app context - e.g. wiring a component into a router, a full page layout, or a provider tree. These are real code the author believes works but Cartograph does not execute or validate them.
language_notes.nim: Use the built-in unittest module for all tests. No echo in src/ files. Mark all public symbols with * (e.g. proc myProc*(x: int): int). Use camelCase for procs and variables, PascalCase for types. Prefer the result variable for return values. A widget_id.nimble file is required at the widget root - it is created by cartograph create and must stay in sync with widget.json dependencies. List nimble package dependencies in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies as 'pkgname >= version'. No quit() or system.exit() in src/ files.

domain_notes.frontend: All appearance values (colors, spacing, typography, shadows) must be exposed as CSS custom properties - hardcoded values lock consumers into your choices. Provide sensible defaults via :root or the component root but every value must be overridable. No inline styles for anything that could vary by theme.
domain_notes.ml: Widgets must be fully validatable without large ML frameworks. Use framework-free implementations (numpy, scikit-learn, plain Python) or API-based inference (HTTP calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace Inference API). torch, tensorflow, jax, and any GPU-dependent code are not permitted - the validation pipeline cannot install or verify hardware-dependent dependencies. If your logic requires a framework, it belongs in your project, not the library.
